  • Monitoring and observability

    ClearML provides integrated monitoring capabilities through its web interface, including real-time GPU utilization dashboards, queue depth and wait time metrics, agent health status, and per-user resource consumption tracking. The dashboard reports GPU utilization across the cluster and can be configured to display up to the maximum number of GPUs in the deployment.

    For integration with existing enterprise monitoring infrastructure, ClearML exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoints that can be scraped by Prometheus and visualized in Grafana dashboards. Key metrics include task queue lengths, agent availability, GPU memory and compute utilization, API server response times, and storage consumption.

    Alerting can be configured through standard Prometheus AlertManager rules or through ClearML's integrated notification framework, which supports Slack, email, and webhook integrations for events such as task failures, agent disconnections, resource quota exhaustion, and deployment health degradation.

    The following table outlines the recommended minimum configuration for ClearML.

    Table 3. Recommended minimum configuration for ClearML
    GPU Count vCPUs RAM Disk
    Up to 16 GPUs 8vCPU 32GB 500GB
    Up to 250 GPUs 3 x 16vCPUs 3x32GB 3 x 4TB

    For planning purposes, organizations should estimate the peak number of concurrent GPU-intensive jobs they expect to run and multiply by the per-job GPU requirement. ClearML's queue-based scheduling and priority management ensure that GPU resources are allocated efficiently, reducing the overprovisioning typically required in unmanaged environments by 40 to 60 percent.

Sizing and scaling

  • Storage sizing

    The standard Dell AI factory configurations include enough local storage to meet the runtime storage requirements for ClearML.

    Storage requirements depend on experiment data volume, model artifact sizes, and dataset management needs. ClearML requires persistent storage for the control plane database, artifact storage, and log retention. This storage is allocated using Kubernetes storage classes, and the underlying storage can be provisioned from the Dell PowerScale storage included in the supported Dell AI factories. ClearML requires separate storage classes for each data service. MongoDB requires a non-NFS storage backend such as block storage (for example, CSI PowerScale). Dragonfly (Redis-compatible), Elasticsearch, and FileServer can use NFS storage. When deploying in external data services mode, persistent volume requirements are managed by the external service deployment rather than the ClearML blueprint. See Appendix A for the full list of storage inputs. Because of the ClearML requirement to run all ClearML services on the kubernetes control-plane node, if PowerScale storage is used, additional configuration of PowerScale drivers is required to allow scheduling on the kubernetes control plane node. See Appendix F for the additional configuration steps.

Sizing and scaling

  • Scaling strategy

    ClearML on Dell AI Factory is designed to scale incrementally. As AI adoption grows, additional GPU nodes can be added to existing Kubernetes clusters and registered with ClearML without reconfiguring the control plane or disrupting running workloads.

    ClearML Agents scale horizontally. Each agent monitors one or more task queues and provisions workloads on available GPU resources. Adding agents to new node pools expands scheduling capacity automatically. Queue-based routing allows different GPU types or tiers to be targeted by workload type, so inference jobs can run on cost-efficient GPUs while training jobs target high-memory accelerators.

    The ClearML control plane services (API server, file server, web server) can be scaled independently using standard Kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaling based on CPU and memory thresholds. For deployments exceeding 100 concurrent users, scaling the API server and Elasticsearch storage is recommended.

    Multi-cluster federation is supported for organizations that operate multiple Dell AI Factory clusters. ClearML provides a unified view across clusters, allowing workloads to be routed to the cluster with available capacity while maintaining centralized experiment tracking and model management.

Sizing and scaling

  • Pilot

    The pilot configuration is designed to run the solution on the minimum resources. The ClearML Platform pilot leverages the Dell PowerEdge R770 or R7725 Servers with Dual RTX 6000 BSE GPUs, enabling teams to validate the workload quickly and establish a clear path to scale. Starting from this baseline, organizations can fully validate the solution for their environment and then move to higher-capacity configurations as adoption grows, with Dell Professional Services available to assist with planning and execution. This approach shortens time-to-value, reduces deployment risk, and standardizes the transition from pilot to production. The standardized deployment model allows organizations to progress from a single lighthouse use case to an enterprise-wide AI Factory without redesigning governance or operational processes.

    The pilot configuration is dedicated to the ClearML workload on the Kubernetes cluster. Red Hat OpenShift will not be compatible with the pilot single-node configuration. In this case, the Dell Automation Platform Orchestrator (DAPO) must run on a separate infrastructure with its own resources.

Solution architecture

  • ClearML on Dell AI Factory is designed as a layered system that separates infrastructure, orchestration, and user interaction. As shown in Figure 1, Dell AI Factory provides the underlying compute, networking, and storage environment, while ClearML delivers an end‑to‑end MLOps and LLMOps platform that operates above the infrastructure layer.

    ClearML operates as an AI as a Service and GPU as a Service offering, providing multi-tenant secure operations and dynamic resource allocation on Dell AI Factory infrastructure. Independent tenants operate in fully isolated environments while sharing the underlying compute, storage, and networking resources.

    ClearML provides five core capabilities across the platform: AIaaS, GPUaaS, AI Repository, AI Management, and LLMOps. These capabilities are available to each tenant independently, with ClearML managing experiment tracking, data and model management, pipeline orchestration, deployment, and monitoring. ClearML serves as the system of control for AI workloads, while remaining independent of specific frameworks, models, or data sources.

    Workload execution occurs on Red Hat OpenShift or Kubernetes clusters running on Dell AI Factory infrastructure. NVIDIA AI Enterprise provides acceleration and supporting software components. Dell Automation Platform manages cluster and workload deployment. The architecture separates management and storage infrastructure (Dell PowerEdge servers for control plane and Dell PowerScale storage) from compute and network infrastructure (Dell PowerSwitch networking and Dell PowerEdge XE and R series servers with NVIDIA GPUs). This separation allows infrastructure, execution, and AI operations to scale independently, while maintaining a single, consistent operational model for enterprise AI workloads.

Solution description

  • ClearML on Dell AI Factory provides a unified platform for operating AI workloads at scale on enterprise infrastructure. ClearML supplies the control plane for experiment tracking, orchestration, pipelines, and resource management, while Dell AI Factory provides validated, GPU‑accelerated infrastructure designed for on‑premises and regulated environments.

    The solution is built for organizations that need to move beyond isolated experimentation and operate AI as a shared, governed capability. ClearML standardizes how models are developed, trained, evaluated, and deployed across teams and frameworks. Dell AI Factory ensures those workflows run reliably on PowerEdge systems with predictable performance and operational support.

    The solution focuses on execution and control rather than abstraction. It enables repeatable AI operations, consistent use of GPU resources, and clear separation of responsibilities between platform teams and AI practitioners. Detailed architecture and deployment mechanics are covered in the following sections.

    What sets this solution apart is the scope of operational control ClearML provides. Unlike point tools that address only scheduling or only experiment tracking, ClearML is the only platform that unifies infrastructure management, AI development workflows, and generative AI application deployment in a single control plane. It supports NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs through a single management layer, eliminating silicon lock-in and giving Dell the flexibility to recommend the right GPU for each workload. ClearML also provides dynamic NVIDIA AI Enterprise license allocation, allowing customers to decouple the number of NVAIE licenses from the number of GPUs in their cluster, reducing initial cost and scaling licenses with demand.

    For organizations operating shared GPU environments, ClearML includes a billing API that automatically tracks compute consumption per team, per user, and per job, enabling chargebacks and cost transparency without manual tracking.

Solution description

  • Benefits

    The solution includes the following benefits:

    Centralized AI operations

    ClearML provides a single system to track experiments, datasets, models, and pipelines across teams. This reduces fragmentation and establishes a shared operational baseline.

    Reproducible development workflows

    Each run captures code, parameters, environments, and artifacts. Results can be compared or rerun without reconstructing context.

    Automated workload orchestration

    Training jobs and pipelines are scheduled and run through queues and agents, removing manual coordination across clusters.

    LLMOps support on enterprise infrastructure

    Fine‑tuning, evaluation, and inference workflows for large language models are managed using the same tracking and orchestration framework, running entirely on Dell AI Factory when required.

    Controlled GPU resource usage

    Queues, quotas, and scheduling policies allow GPUs to be shared across teams with predictable access and usage visibility.

    Enterprise security and deployment flexibility

    Role‑based access control, audit logging, and support for on‑premises and air‑gapped deployments align the platform with enterprise security and compliance requirements.

    Simplified deployment and support model

    Availability as a Dell Automation Platform blueprint and a joint Dell and ClearML support model reduce deployment effort and clarify operational ownership.

    Silicon-agnostic GPU management

    ClearML manages NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs through a single orchestration layer. This eliminates vendor lock-in and allows Dell customers to select the optimal GPU for each workload without changing the management platform.

    Dynamic NVIDIA AI Enterprise license management

    ClearML dynamically allocates NVAIE licenses across the GPU cluster in real time. Customers can deploy more GPUs than licenses, with ClearML managing allocation based on actual NIM and NVAIE workload demand. This reduces initial licensing costs and scales with usage.

    Integrated chargeback and cost transparency

    The ClearML billing API automatically tracks GPU consumption per team, user, and job. Finance teams gain visibility into AI spending by business unit, enabling chargebacks and justifying infrastructure investment without manual tracking or spreadsheet reconciliation.

    Multi-tenant isolation and governance

    Multiple teams or business units can operate on shared Dell AI Factory infrastructure with full tenant isolation. Each tenant receives a dedicated environment with its own compute agents, application gateway, and access controls, managed through a centralized deployment model. Each tenant maintains independent identity management and access controls while sharing the underlying infrastructure.

Summary

  • AI programs fail less often because of modeling limits and more often because of operational friction. This guide started from that reality. It described why experimentation alone does not scale, why infrastructure without control creates new bottlenecks, and why enterprises need a consistent way to operate AI across teams, models, and environments.

    You have seen how ClearML on Dell AI Factory addresses these problems by establishing a clear operating model. The document walked through the business challenges that emerge as AI adoption grows, the use cases that expose those challenges, and the architecture that supports repeatable execution. It explained how experiments become traceable, pipelines replace manual handoffs, GPU resources are governed, and LLM workflows are treated as first‑class operational assets. It also showed how multi-tenant isolation enables independent organizations to operate on shared infrastructure with full separation of resources, credentials, and access controls. The guide then covered how this model is deployed, secured, and supported in enterprise environments.

    The result is not a new toolchain, but a stable foundation for AI delivery. One where platform teams retain control, practitioners retain flexibility, and AI work moves forward with fewer resets and fewer exceptions. This is the shift from isolated success to sustained execution.

    To learn more about deploying ClearML on Dell AI Factory, or to discuss how this solution fits your environment, contact your Dell Technologies sales representative or go to Dell Technologies to continue the conversation.

Supported Dell AI Factory infrastructure

  • ClearML is deployed on Dell AI Factory, which provides validated, GPU-accelerated infrastructure for enterprise AI workloads. The platform supports Kubernetes-based execution, high‑throughput networking, and persistent storage required for large‑scale model training, pipelines, and inference. ClearML relies on this foundation for compute and connectivity, while remaining agnostic to the specific AI frameworks and data platforms used above it.
